title: Predictive Analytics with SAP and Snowflake: Use Cases
summary: See how SAP and Snowflake's zero-copy integration powers predictive analytics for demand forecasting, fraud detection and customer churn reduction.
body_markdown:
Your SAP system knows your business better than almost any other system. It tracks every transaction, every shipment, every invoice and every customer interaction. Yet for most organizations, combining that operational data with the rest of their data estate to drive predictive insights has required extracting it, rebuilding its business context and stitching it together with data from other systems — a process so slow and fragile that many predictive initiatives never make it past the pilot stage.


[SAP and Snowflake](https://www.snowflake.com/en/why-snowflake/partners/all-partners/sap/) 's[zero-copy integration](https://www.snowflake.com/en/blog/sap-snowflake-zero-copy-integration-enterprise-ai/) changes this. Using SAP Business Data Cloud (BDC) Connect for Snowflake, organizations can access semantically rich SAP data products in near real time — without copying, moving or duplicating data — and unify them with non-SAP data to power machine learning models and agents to answer a broader set of questions grounded in all enterprise data that drive real business outcomes.


Here's how it works in practice across three high-impact use cases.


## Use case 1: Demand forecasting for supply chain


Supply chain teams have always wanted to predict demand. The challenge is that accurate forecasting requires more than historical sales data from SAP. It needs context: Internet of Things (IoT) sensor readings from warehouses, logistics partner data, weather patterns, macroeconomic indicators and competitor signals.


With SAP and Snowflake, teams build a unified supply chain data model that brings semantically rich SAP data together with IoT, logistics and external signals. Predictive AI models can then forecast demand, lead times and supply risk using the full picture, not just the SAP slice.


The results go beyond better forecasts. Organizations can run spend analytics to reduce inventory costs, score suppliers on risk, sense demand shifts in near real time and dynamically reroute shipments when disruptions occur. Snowflake Marketplace provides access to third-party data sets — weather, risk indices and macroeconomic data — that enrich the predictive models without additional integration work.


## Use case 2: Fraud detection for financial services


Financial institutions run on SAP for core processes such as accounts payable, general ledger and profitability analysis. But fraud detection requires pattern recognition across far more than ERP data. It needs customer relationship management (CRM) pipeline data, market conditions, vendor histories, transaction anomalies and external benchmarks.


Snowflake unifies these data silos with SAP financial data to create a comprehensive view for AI-driven risk detection. Snowflake Cortex AI provides variance analysis and forecasting capabilities that flag anomalies automatically — for example, identifying vendor invoices outside normal spending ranges and quantifying the potential financial risk.


Because the models run inside Snowflake's governed environment, sensitive financial data doesn’t leave the security perimeter. Cortex Agents can orchestrate multistep investigations — query structured ERP data for transaction patterns, pull unstructured data such as call center transcripts or claims reports, and generate findings — all within a single governed workflow. State-of-the-art LLMs from Anthropic, OpenAI and others are brought to the data, not the other way around, reducing egress costs and maintaining compliance.


The approach extends beyond fraud. The same unified foundation supports predictive forecasting for financial close processes, scenario planning with AI-based revenue prediction and enterprise KPI harmonization — capabilities particularly valuable for CFO organizations.


## Use case 3: Customer churn reduction


Every customer interaction — whether it happens in an SAP ERP solution, a CRM platform, a mobile app or a support ticket — generates a signal about churn risk. But most organizations can't unify those signals fast enough to act on them.


SAP and Snowflake can create a customer 360 that spans SAP S/4HANA, CRM, product usage telemetry, digital interactions and subscription data. Predictive models built on this unified view can identify at-risk customers before they leave, recommend next best actions and trigger personalized retention offers — all driven by Cortex AI.


Supply chain managers can ask "Which customers are most likely to churn this quarter?" and get an answer grounded in unified SAP, CRM and usage data with no data science team required. Native governance capabilities protect sensitive customer and revenue data throughout the process. And because the integration is bidirectional, insights generated in Snowflake can be made available back in SAP BDC for activation — closing the loop between prediction and action.


## How to implement


The implementation path is intentionally straightforward:


1. **Connect:** Existing Snowflake customers can activate SAP BDC Connect for Snowflake to access SAP data products — no pipelines and ETL needed.
2. **Unify:** SAP data products — carrying business semantics such as Customer, Product and General Ledger — become available through BDC Connect, alongside non-SAP data in Snowflake. No semantic reconstruction is needed.
3. **Model:** Build and train predictive models using Snowpark — or skip the code entirely with Cortex AI for automated insights. Models run where the data lives, with no data movement and no external tooling.
4. **Enrich:** Pull external data from Snowflake Marketplace — weather, macroeconomic data and industry benchmarks — to strengthen model accuracy.
5. **Activate:** Publish predictions and insights back to SAP BDC for operational activation, creating a closed loop from data to insight to action.


The entire process — including data access, model development, deployment, governance and activation — is governed end to end within Snowflake's security perimeter. There’s no fragmented tooling, no pipeline maintenance and no governance gaps.


## The bottom line


Predictive analytics has always promised more than it delivered for SAP customers. SAP captures extraordinarily rich business semantics. Snowflake makes those semantics available for[cross-system analytics and AI](https://www.snowflake.com/en/webinars/thought-leadership/sap-and-snowflake-unlock-the-full-power-of-data-and-enterprise-ai-2026-07-29/) — together, they unlock value that neither could deliver alone.


SAP and Snowflake's zero-copy integration means SAP data stays where it is, retains its semantics and becomes available for ML alongside the rest of the enterprise. The result is predictive analytics that actually works — and is faster to build, more accurate to run and easier to operationalize.
